title: Add RawString support to preserve original string escaping if any
body:
## Add `kParseRawStringsFlag` for preserving original string escape sequences during SAX round-trip

### Problem

When using RapidJSON's SAX pipeline (Reader → Writer/PrettyWriter), all string escape sequences are decoded during parsing and re-encoded during writing. This means:

- `\u003C` (escaped `<`) becomes literal `<`
- `\/` (escaped `/`) becomes literal `/`
- `\u4e16\u754c` (escaped CJK) becomes literal UTF-8 bytes

While semantically equivalent per RFC 8259, this normalization is undesirable in tools like JSON formatters where users expect their original escape representation to be preserved.

RapidJSON already has `kParseNumbersAsStringsFlag` + `RawNumber()` for preserving raw number text. This PR adds the equivalent for strings.

### Changes

**reader.h**
- Added `kParseRawStringsFlag = 1024` to `ParseFlag` enum
- Added `RawString()` / `RawKey()` to the Handler concept and `BaseReaderHandler` (with fallback to `String()` / `Key()`)
- Modified `ParseString()`: when flag is set, captures raw content between quotes using stream positions after full validation, then calls `handler.RawString()` / `handler.RawKey()` via `if constexpr` (avoids instantiation for handlers that don't implement these methods, like `GenericDocument`)

**writer.h**
- Added `RawString()`, `RawKey()`, and `WriteRawString()` — outputs raw content wrapped in quotes without re-encoding

**prettywriter.h**
- Added `RawString()` and `RawKey()` with `PrettyPrefix` for proper indentation

### Design

- Full validation still runs — `ParseStringToStream` decodes and validates every character before the raw path extracts content. Invalid escapes, lone surrogates, and unterminated strings still produce errors.
- Raw content is extracted from the source stream via `head_` pointer + `Tell()` positions — no additional buffering needed.
- No changes to `document.h` or the DOM path. `kRawStringFlag` is not needed because (unlike numbers) strings don't have a JSON-structural ambiguity — `RawString` and `String` both produce quoted strings.
- Only works in non-insitu mode (insitu path falls back to decoded `String()`/`Key()`).

### Tests

Added to existing RapidJSON test files:

- **readertest.cpp**: 11 tests — custom `RawStringsHandler` verifying Unicode escapes, `\/`, standard escapes, surrogate pairs, empty strings, arrays, keys, combined flags, and validation error preservation
- **writertest.cpp**: 5 tests — `RawString`, `RawKey`, escaped slash, empty string, full round-trip
- **prettywritertest.cpp**: 4 tests — `RawString`, `RawKey`, round-trip with pretty formatting

### Note

This code and tests were prepared with AI assistance (GitHub Copilot / Claude).

## What is this PR?

This PR fixes a crash that I encountered.

`Schema::Schema` processes dependencies arrays by calling `FindPropertyIndex` on each element to look up property names. `FindPropertyIndex` calls `GetStringLength`, which asserts `IsString`, but the spec does not forbid non-string elements in a dependencies array, so a schema like `{"dependencies":{"a":[0,2]}}` caused an assertion failure (`SIGABRT`).

title: Respect riscv targets in platform macros
body:
## Why

RapidJSON is header-only, but some platform macros and test/performance entry points still infer target capabilities from host compiler predefined macros. In a simulated or cross-target `riscv64` configuration built from an `x86_64` host compiler, that can incorrectly preserve x86-only assumptions such as the 48-bit pointer optimization or host SIMD auto-detection. This patch makes the generic RISC-V path explicit and keeps simulated validation builds from inheriting host-specific SIMD behavior.

## What changed

- Add a conservative `RAPIDJSON_RISCV` platform macro in `rapidjson.h`.
- Treat `__riscv_xlen == 64` as a 64-bit target in `rapidjson.h`.
- Disable `RAPIDJSON_48BITPOINTER_OPTIMIZATION` on RISC-V so RISC-V builds do not inherit the x86-64-specific pointer compression assumption.
- Update `test/perftest/perftest.h` and `test/unittest/simdtest.cpp` so simulated or cross-target RISC-V validation does not auto-enable host `SSE2`/`SSE4.2`/`NEON` paths.
- Adjust the tutorial example to use a dynamically built `std::string`, avoiding an x86-specific short-string layout assumption during non-x86 validation builds.

## Verification

- Ran native CMake configuration with Ninja using `RAPIDJSON_BUILD_DOC=OFF` and `RAPIDJSON_BUILD_TESTS=OFF`.
- Built the native examples successfully with `cmake --build build-codex-native-058 --parallel 4`.
- Ran simulated `riscv64` CMake configuration with `CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux`, `CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64`, `CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_TARGET_TYPE=STATIC_LIBRARY`, and forced `__riscv=1` / `__riscv_xlen=64` because no real RISC-V toolchain is available on the host.
- Preprocessed `rapidjson.h` under forced `__riscv=1` / `__riscv_xlen=64` and confirmed `RAPIDJSON_RISCV=1`, `RAPIDJSON_64BIT=1`, and `RAPIDJSON_48BITPOINTER_OPTIMIZATION=0`.
- Built the simulated example sources to object files, including `example/tutorial/tutorial.cpp.o`, and confirmed `build.ninja` contains no `-msse*`, `-mavx*`, or `NEON` flags.

## Notes

This is a conservative portability patch. It does not add a RISC-V SIMD backend. Because the host environment uses a Windows-native compiler while simulating a Linux `riscv64` target, the final executable link step still inherits a host/toolchain mismatch around `-rdynamic`. Verification therefore focuses on native example build stability, simulated RISC-V configuration, object compilation, macro checks, and x86/ARM SIMD flag exclusion rather than a full real `riscv64` link.

title: Fix out-of-bounds operand-stack pop in regex kConcatenation eval
body:
## Bug

`GenericRegex::Eval()`'s `kConcatenation` case pops two `Frag` operands off the operand stack unconditionally, guarding it only with `RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(operandStack.GetSize() >= sizeof(Frag) * 2)`. In `NDEBUG` (release) builds this assert compiles out, so a malformed pattern that reaches `kConcatenation` with fewer than two operands on the stack pops past the start of the stack.

Every other multi-operand case in the same function (`kAlternation`, `kZeroOrOne`, `kZeroOrMore`, `kOneOrMore`) already guards this with an `if` and returns `false` on underflow, which `GenericRegex`'s caller turns into a `kRegexInvalidState` — surfaced by `SchemaValidator::CreatePattern()` as a `RegexInvalid` schema error rather than a crash. `kConcatenation` was the one case that never got this treatment.

Reported in #2373 as an assertion failure in the regex engine (repro: schema `{"pattern":"^s(}}}|)}}}}}}}}+\"}` validated against any document). That issue's own analysis pointed at `kAlternation`, but that case was already fixed this same way back in 2021 (89f6717c) — it's not reachable with the reported input. Reproducing the issue's own input against current `master` shows the actual live crash is in `kConcatenation`, at a different point in `Eval()` than the issue described.

## Fix

Mirror the existing guarded pattern used by the sibling cases: check the stack size before popping, and return `false` (rather than asserting) when it's underpopulated.

## Testing

- Added `SchemaValidator.Issue2373` in `test/unittest/schematest.cpp`, using the same `SCHEMAERROR`/`RegexInvalid` assertion style as the existing `String_Pattern_Invalid` test for another malformed-pattern case.
- Confirmed the new test fails (throws the `operandStack.GetSize() >= sizeof(Frag) * 2` assertion) against `master` without this fix, and passes with it.
- Ran the full local unit test suite (`test/unittest`, built via CMake with `RAPIDJSON_BUILD_TESTS=ON`): 470/470 tests pass, including all `SchemaValidator`/`Schema` and `Regex`-prefixed tests.

title: reader: reject fractions long enough to underflow expFrac (#2391)
body:
Fix for #2391.

### What's happening

`ParseNumber` in `include/rapidjson/reader.h` decrements `expFrac`
once per fraction digit, in two loops, with no upper bound on how far
`expFrac` can go negative. For an all-zeros fraction the significand
never grows, so the fast-path `if (i64 > 2^53-1) break` never fires
and the loop just keeps decrementing until the stream ends.

At ~2 147 483 341 fraction digits, `--expFrac` wraps past `INT_MIN`
(UB #1), and the follow-up

```cpp
int maxExp = 308 - expFrac;   // reader.h:1667
```

then overflows `INT_MAX` (UB #2). The `(expFrac + 2 147 483 639) / 10`
maxExp in the negative-exponent branch has the same shape.

Under UBSan with `-fno-sanitize-recover=all` the reproducer aborts on:

include/rapidjson/reader.h:1667:25: runtime error:
signed integer overflow: 308 - -2147483341 cannot be represented in type 'int'


### The change

Add a cheap bound just before each `--expFrac`:

```cpp
if (RAPIDJSON_UNLIKELY(expFrac <= (std::numeric_limits<int>::min)() + 500))
    RAPIDJSON_PARSE_ERROR(kParseErrorNumberTooBig, startOffset);
```

Any real JSON number keeps `expFrac` in a very small range, so this
only rejects pathological input; when it fires the parse fails
cleanly with `kParseErrorNumberTooBig`, the same way the exponent
side already handles out-of-range values.

`+8 / −0`, `include/rapidjson/reader.h` only.

### How it was verified

Against upstream `master` at `24b5e7a` on Linux x86_64:

- Reproducer: `"0." + 2 147 483 340 × '0' + "1e5"` streamed through
  `FileReadStream`, `Document::ParseStream`, harness compiled with
  `-fsanitize=undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all`.
- Baseline: UBSan trap at `reader.h:1667:25` with
  `308 - -2147483341 cannot be represented in type 'int'`.
- With this change: parse returns
  `kParseErrorNumberTooBig` — "Number too big to be stored in
  double." — at offset 0. No UBSan hits anywhere in the run.
- Regression: `3.141592653589793e2` still parses; `"0." + 1 000 × '0'
  + "1e5"` still parses. The guard only fires on inputs that would
  otherwise UB.

### Threshold math (why 500 is a safe margin)

`INT_MIN = -2 147 483 648`. After the guard passes, `expFrac` can be
as low as `INT_MIN + 501` immediately before `--expFrac`, so its
worst-case value in the subsequent maxExp computations is
`INT_MIN + 500`. Then `308 - (INT_MIN + 500) = 2 147 483 456`, which
is comfortably below `INT_MAX = 2 147 483 647`. `(expFrac +
2 147 483 639) / 10` at the same point is `(-2 147 483 148 + 2 147 483 639) / 10 = 49`.

### Reporter

Thanks to @nvartolomei — the report pinpoints both UB sites and the
exact reproducer input, which is what let this ship as an 8-line
change.

### AI assistance

I used an AI assistant to help draft the change, the reproduction and
this description. Every line was read, checked and run by me.

- [x] I have re-read every line and this description is in my own words.

title: Fix integer overflow in Writer::WriteString for long strings
body:
Fixes #2348, and the same root cause reported separately in #2336.

`WriteString` computes the stack reservation as `2 + length * 6` (or `* 12` for the non-Unicode-target case), where `length` is a `SizeType`. With the default `SizeType` (`unsigned`, 32-bit), that multiplication overflows for strings around 716 million characters and up, so `PutReserve` ends up reserving far less space than the writer actually needs. Once writing continues past the undersized buffer, that's either a hard assertion failure in `Stack::PushUnsafe` in debug builds (exactly the crash reported in #2348), or plain memory corruption in release builds.

Widening `length` to `size_t` before the multiplication fixes it: on 64-bit platforms the multiplication now happens at 64 bits and can't wrap around for any length that actually fits in a `SizeType` to begin with.

Verified with a small standalone program writing an 800,000,000-character string through `Writer<StringBuffer>`: reliably hits the reported assertion on unmodified master, and completes correctly with the fix (produces a `StringBuffer` of the exact expected size). I didn't add this as an automated unit test in this PR, since a real repro needs close to a gigabyte of memory and I wasn't sure that's a good tradeoff for the test suite to run on every CI job — happy to add one if you'd rather have it. Ran the existing writer, prettywriter, stringbuffer, and document unit tests (63 cases) against the fix, all pass unchanged.
